catalogue.title: Pasteur Network Climate and Health Metadata Catalogue
catalogue.subtitle: Shared descriptions of the climate, environmental and health datasets used in Pasteur Network climate and health research
catalogue.maintainer: Mauro César Cafundó de Morais, Climate and Health Laboratory, IPSP
catalogue.purpose: The catalogue records, for every dataset a contributing institute uses or needs, what it contains, its spatial and temporal resolution, how often it is updated, who holds it, and the conditions under which it can be shared. It does not centralise or open the data. Describing the data consistently is enough to make it usable, and removes the slowest part of the work: finding out what exists and who to ask.

sources.label: Health data: Portal de Dados Abertos do SUS
Climate data: Copernicus Climate Data Store (CDS)

projects.name: Yellow fever and minimum temperature anomalies
projects.question: Do runs of unusually warm nights precede yellow fever transmission in the Brazilian Southeast?
projects.extent: Southeast Brazil (SP, MG, RJ, ES) - 1,668 municipalities, 2016-2025

projects.name: Dengue and urban heat islands in São Paulo
projects.question: Does neighbourhood-level heat exposure explain where dengue clusters within the municipality of São Paulo?
projects.unit: Census sector or weather-station catchment x epidemiological week

projects.name: American cutaneous leishmaniasis and climate in the Amazon
projects.question: Which climate and land-use conditions predict ACL incidence in the Amazonian biome?

datasets.title: SINAN - Yellow fever notifications
datasets.description: Individual notification records of suspected and confirmed human yellow fever, including notification and symptom-onset dates, municipality of residence and of probable infection, case classification and outcome.
datasets.key_variables: Notification date; symptom onset date; municipality of residence (IBGE 6-digit); municipality of probable infection; final classification; evolution/death; vaccination status
datasets.custodian: Ministério da Saúde / DATASUS (national); state and municipal surveillance secretariats feed the system
datasets.producer: Sistema de Informação de Agravos de Notificação (SINAN)
datasets.contact: Portal de Dados Abertos do SUS - dadosabertos.saude.gov.br
datasets.native_resolution: Individual record, geocoded to municipality of residence and of probable infection
datasets.temporal_resolution: Daily (event dates), aggregated to epidemiological week
datasets.update_frequency: Continuous notification; public files consolidated annually, preliminary files updated more often
datasets.latency: Weeks to months for preliminary data; ~1 year for closed annual files
datasets.licence: Open government data (Lei de Acesso à Informação); attribution to MS/SVSA expected
datasets.sharing_conditions: Public de-identified files may be redistributed. Identified line-lists require a data-use agreement with the surveillance authority and ethics approval.
datasets.personal_data: Public files de-identified; municipality of residence retained
datasets.linkage_key: IBGE municipality code (6-digit in health files; divide 7-digit code by 10 to match)
datasets.limitations: Under-notification in low-access areas; municipality of probable infection is often missing or inferred; retrospective reclassification changes historical counts.

datasets.title: SINAN - Dengue notifications
datasets.description: Individual notification records of suspected and confirmed dengue, with symptom-onset date, municipality of residence, laboratory results, serotype where typed, severity classification and outcome.
datasets.key_variables: Symptom onset date; notification date; municipality and district of residence; serotype; laboratory confirmation; severity; hospitalisation; evolution
datasets.custodian: Ministério da Saúde / DATASUS; municipal data flow through COVISA in São Paulo
datasets.producer: Sistema de Informação de Agravos de Notificação (SINAN)
datasets.contact: Portal de Dados Abertos do SUS - dadosabertos.saude.gov.br
datasets.spatial_coverage: Brazil (analysis subset: municipality of São Paulo)
datasets.native_resolution: Individual record; public files resolve to municipality only
datasets.analysis_unit: Municipality (public files); census sector (restricted COVISA extract, see HEA-003)
datasets.temporal_resolution: Daily event dates, aggregated to epidemiological week
datasets.update_frequency: Continuous notification; annual consolidated files, weekly preliminary panels
datasets.latency: 1-4 weeks for preliminary counts; ~1 year for closed files
datasets.licence: Open government data; attribution to MS/SVSA expected
datasets.sharing_conditions: Public files redistributable. Sub-municipal geography is not in the public release and must be requested from COVISA.
datasets.limitations: Public geography stops at the municipality, which is too coarse for a heat-island analysis; serotype typed for a small subset of cases.

datasets.title: COVISA arbovirus surveillance line-list, São Paulo
datasets.title_pt: Vigilância de arboviroses - COVISA, Município de São Paulo
datasets.description: Municipal arbovirus surveillance records for São Paulo with residential address geocoding, allowing cases to be assigned to census sectors, districts and weather-station catchments. Includes the subset of cases with a laboratory-confirmed serotype.
datasets.key_variables: Geocoded residence (point or census sector); symptom onset date; case classification; serotype for laboratory-typed cases; age; sex
datasets.custodian: COVISA - Coordenadoria de Vigilância em Saúde, Secretaria Municipal da Saúde de São Paulo
datasets.contact: To be confirmed - COVISA arbovirus surveillance division
datasets.native_resolution: Address point, aggregated to census sector or district for release
datasets.update_frequency: Weekly internally; release schedule to be agreed
datasets.formats: CSV or database extract, to be agreed
datasets.licence: Not applicable - governed by the data-use agreement
datasets.sharing_conditions: Requires CEP/CONEP ethics approval, then a formal data-sharing agreement with COVISA. Aggregated outputs only; no address-level redistribution; publication drafts shared with COVISA before submission.
datasets.personal_data: Yes - geocoded residence is potentially identifying. Aggregate to census sector before analysis and suppress small counts.
datasets.linkage_key: IBGE census sector code (2022); epidemiological week
datasets.limitations: Geocoding completeness varies by year and by neighbourhood; small-area counts require suppression rules.
datasets.holding_status: To be acquired - awaiting ethics approval, then confirmation with COVISA
datasets.record_status: Draft - confirm with COVISA once ethics approval is granted

datasets.title: SINAN - American cutaneous leishmaniasis notifications
datasets.description: Individual notification records of American cutaneous leishmaniasis, with clinical form, municipality of residence and of probable infection, diagnostic criteria, treatment and outcome.
datasets.key_variables: Notification and onset dates; municipality of residence and probable infection; clinical form (cutaneous/mucosal); diagnostic criterion; treatment; evolution; occupation
datasets.custodian: Ministério da Saúde / DATASUS; Secretaria de Estado da Saúde do Pará
datasets.producer: Sistema de Informação de Agravos de Notificação (SINAN)
datasets.contact: Portal de Dados Abertos do SUS - dadosabertos.saude.gov.br
datasets.native_resolution: Individual record, municipality of residence and of probable infection
datasets.temporal_resolution: Daily event dates, aggregated to month
datasets.licence: Open government data; attribution to MS/SVSA expected
datasets.sharing_conditions: Public de-identified files may be redistributed with attribution.
datasets.limitations: Place of infection frequently differs from place of residence in a mobile rural population; under-diagnosis in areas with limited health-service access.

datasets.title: SI-PNI immunisation coverage
datasets.description: Doses administered and coverage estimates by municipality, age group and immunobiological, including yellow fever and dengue vaccines. Used as a confounder and as denominator context.
datasets.key_variables: Doses applied; immunobiological; dose number; age group; municipality; administration date
datasets.custodian: Ministério da Saúde / DATASUS - Programa Nacional de Imunizações
datasets.producer: Sistema de Informação do Programa Nacional de Imunizações (SI-PNI)
datasets.contact: Portal de Dados Abertos do SUS - dadosabertos.saude.gov.br
datasets.native_resolution: Municipality (aggregate); individual dose records in the nominal system
datasets.licence: Open government data
datasets.sharing_conditions: Redistributable with attribution.
datasets.limitations: Coverage denominators rely on population projections that drifted from the 2022 census; campaign doses can be recorded late.

datasets.title: Non-human primate epizootic records
datasets.title_pt: Vigilância de epizootias em primatas não humanos
datasets.description: Reports of sickness or death in non-human primates investigated for yellow fever, the earliest available signal of sylvatic virus circulation and therefore a candidate outcome ahead of human cases.
datasets.key_variables: Event date; municipality; species; laboratory result; classification
datasets.custodian: Ministério da Saúde / SVSA; state surveillance; SISS-Geo (Fiocruz) for citizen reports
datasets.update_frequency: Continuous, with reporting peaks during outbreaks
datasets.licence: To be confirmed
datasets.sharing_conditions: To be confirmed with SVSA and Fiocruz.
datasets.limitations: Strongly effort-dependent - reporting rises where surveillance teams are active and during known outbreaks, so absence is not evidence of absence.

datasets.title: ERA5-Land reanalysis - daily surface variables
datasets.title_pt: Reanálise ERA5-Land - variáveis diárias de superfície
datasets.description: Global land-surface climate reconstruction. The laboratory downloads minimum, mean and maximum 2 m air temperature, total precipitation, 2 m dew-point temperature, 10 m wind components and surface pressure, then reduces each to one value per municipality.
datasets.key_variables: Tmin, Tmean, Tmax (2 m); total precipitation; dew-point temperature; 10 m U and V wind; surface pressure
datasets.custodian: European Centre for Medium-Range Weather Forecasts, through the Copernicus Climate Data Store
datasets.contact: Copernicus Climate Data Store, registered account and API key
datasets.temporal_resolution: Hourly native; downloaded daily, aggregated to epidemiological week (YF, dengue) or month (ACL)
datasets.update_frequency: Rolling, about 2-3 months behind real time
datasets.licence: Copernicus licence - free reuse with attribution
datasets.sharing_conditions: Raw data freely redistributable under the Copernicus licence. Derived municipality series may be published with attribution.
datasets.limitations: Temperatures arrive in Kelvin (subtract 273.15). A reanalysis is a model product, not a measurement, and 9 km cannot resolve within-city heat contrasts - use CLI-004 for that. Coastal and steep-terrain municipalities are least reliable. The Pará download was extended to dew-point temperature in August 2026; series before that date do not contain it.

datasets.title: ERA5-Land weekly climatological normals
datasets.title_pt: Normais climatológicas semanais derivadas do ERA5-Land
datasets.description: Pre-computed long-term weekly averages per municipality, used as the reference against which any week of any year is called normal or anomalous.
datasets.key_variables: Weekly normals for Tmin (1981-2010 and 1991-2020), Tmax, precipitation, relative humidity and wind speed (1981-2010)
datasets.custodian: IPSP Climate and Health Laboratory (derived); ERA5-Land upstream
datasets.update_frequency: Recomputed when the baseline period changes (roughly every decade)
datasets.access_url: Internal repository; see DER-001 for the published equivalents
datasets.licence: To be assigned - CC BY 4.0 proposed
datasets.sharing_conditions: Shareable with partners on request; publish alongside the paper.
datasets.linkage_key: IBGE municipality code; ISO week number
datasets.limitations: The choice of baseline changes the answer. The 1991-2020 normal is warmer and flags anomalies more conservatively than 1981-2010; state which baseline is used in every output.

datasets.title: Large-scale climate indices - ENSO, IOD, PDO
datasets.description: Single global time series describing El Niño-Southern Oscillation, the Indian Ocean Dipole and the Pacific Decadal Oscillation, used as background drivers common to all municipalities.
datasets.key_variables: ENSO index; IOD index; PDO index
datasets.custodian: Obtained through the InfoDengue Sprint 2024-25 dataset; original indices from NOAA and equivalent agencies
datasets.producer: NOAA and partner agencies, redistributed by InfoDengue
datasets.analysis_unit: One value per week, applied nationally
datasets.update_frequency: Weekly to monthly depending on index
datasets.access_url: InfoDengue Sprint dataset; NOAA for originals
datasets.licence: Open, attribution to originating agency
datasets.sharing_conditions: Redistributable with attribution.
datasets.limitations: No spatial contrast, so these can only explain shared year-to-year variation, not why one municipality differs from its neighbour.

datasets.title: CGE/CGESP municipal weather-station network, São Paulo
datasets.title_pt: Rede de estações meteorológicas do CGE - Município de São Paulo
datasets.description: The municipal network of automatic weather and rainfall stations operated by São Paulo's climate emergency management centre. This is the only source fine enough to separate hot from cool neighbourhoods inside the city, which is what the heat-island analysis needs.
datasets.key_variables: Air temperature; relative humidity; rainfall; wind; station coordinates and installation history
datasets.custodian: CGE - Centro de Gerenciamento de Emergências Climáticas, Prefeitura de São Paulo
datasets.contact: To be confirmed - CGE technical division
datasets.native_resolution: Point stations; station density and catchment size to be documented
datasets.analysis_unit: Station catchment or interpolated surface, joined to census sectors
datasets.temporal_resolution: Sub-hourly to hourly, aggregated to daily and weekly
datasets.update_frequency: Continuous, near real time on the public portal
datasets.latency: Minutes for the live portal; archive access to be confirmed
datasets.formats: To be confirmed - web portal, possible CSV export
datasets.licence: To be confirmed
datasets.sharing_conditions: To be agreed with CGE at project start, together with archive access, the station history file and the citation terms. Expect attribution and possibly an acknowledgement or co-authorship arrangement for the historical archive.
datasets.limitations: Stations are unevenly distributed and periphery coverage is thinner than the centre, which risks under-measuring the hottest and most dengue-affected areas. Record gaps and instrument changes need a station-history file.
datasets.holding_status: To be acquired - terms agreed at project start
datasets.record_status: Draft - confirm with CGE at project start

datasets.title: INMET automatic station network
datasets.title_pt: Rede de estações automáticas do INMET
datasets.description: The national network of automatic surface stations. Its role here is validation: it is the ground measurement used to quantify the bias in the ERA5-Land reanalysis (CLI-001), municipality by municipality, with particular attention to Pará where stations are sparse.
datasets.key_variables: Air temperature (instantaneous, max, min); relative humidity; precipitation; wind; pressure; radiation
datasets.custodian: INMET - Instituto Nacional de Meteorologia
datasets.spatial_coverage: Brazil - station network, sparse in the Amazon
datasets.analysis_unit: Station, matched to the containing municipality
datasets.licence: Open government data, attribution to INMET
datasets.sharing_conditions: Redistributable with attribution.
datasets.linkage_key: Station code and coordinates; IBGE municipality code; date
datasets.limitations: Very sparse in Pará, so the bias estimate will have wide uncertainty over much of the ACL study area, and that uncertainty should be reported rather than smoothed over. Gaps and sensor changes are common and are not always flagged in the files.
datasets.holding_status: To be acquired - bias quantification against ERA5-Land

datasets.title: ANA hydrological station network (HidroWeb)
datasets.description: River stage and discharge measured at gauging stations on Amazonian rivers. This is the measured alternative to using extreme rainfall as a stand-in for flooding: a river level above its flood reference is an observation, not an inference.
datasets.key_variables: River stage (cm); discharge (m3/s); rainfall at co-located gauges; flood reference level
datasets.custodian: ANA - Agência Nacional de Águas e Saneamento Básico
datasets.producer: ANA, with state and utility operators
datasets.contact: HidroWeb portal and the ANA API
datasets.spatial_coverage: Brazil - station network; denser on main Amazonian channels than on tributaries
datasets.analysis_unit: Station, assigned to downstream municipalities in its catchment
datasets.temporal_coverage: Varies by station; many Amazonian records run from the 1970s
datasets.temporal_resolution: Daily stage readings; sub-daily at telemetric stations
datasets.update_frequency: Daily to near real time at telemetric stations
datasets.latency: Hours at telemetric stations; months for validated historical series
datasets.licence: Open government data, attribution to ANA
datasets.sharing_conditions: Redistributable with attribution.
datasets.linkage_key: Station code with coordinates; IBGE municipality code of the catchment; date
datasets.limitations: A gauge measures the river, not the floodplain. Stations sit on main channels, so flooding in small tributary settlements - where ACL transmission concentrates - may not register. Assess coverage against the case municipalities before committing.
datasets.holding_status: Candidate - under assessment for the inundation layer

datasets.title: MODIS vegetation greenness (NDVI)
datasets.description: Satellite measure of how green and dense vegetation is. Two variants are held: a ~1 km series obtained through NASA AppEEARS for the yellow fever work, and the 250 m MOD13Q1 product obtained through Google Earth Engine for the leishmaniasis work.
datasets.key_variables: NDVI (maximum, mean, minimum, standard deviation per municipality)
datasets.custodian: NASA - LP DAAC, accessed through AppEEARS and Google Earth Engine
datasets.spatial_coverage: Global; downloaded for Brazil (YF) and Pará (ACL)
datasets.licence: NASA open data, attribution requested
datasets.sharing_conditions: Redistributable with attribution.
datasets.limitations: Persistent cloud in the Amazon thins the usable composites. Monthly NDVI is joined onto a weekly panel in the YF work, so the greenness value repeats across weeks within a month.

datasets.title: MapBiomas land cover and land use
datasets.title_pt: MapBiomas - cobertura e uso da terra
datasets.description: Annual national land-cover map from Landsat imagery. Supplies forest cover and fragmentation for the yellow fever work, and areas of deforestation, secondary regrowth, agriculture and water for the leishmaniasis work.
datasets.key_variables: Class areas per municipality-year: forest, secondary vegetation, agriculture, pasture, urban, water; derived fragmentation metrics
datasets.custodian: MapBiomas project (Brazilian civil-society and academic network)
datasets.native_resolution: 30 m (Landsat); municipality statistics also distributed pre-summarised
datasets.analysis_unit: Municipality x year (percentage or hectares per class)
datasets.update_frequency: Annual, with a new collection roughly every year
datasets.licence: CC BY-SA 4.0
datasets.sharing_conditions: Redistributable under CC BY-SA with attribution to MapBiomas and the collection number.
datasets.limitations: Collections are reprocessed retrospectively, so a series downloaded today will not match one downloaded two years ago. Always record the collection number.

datasets.title: Built-up surface index (NDBI)
datasets.description: Satellite measure of how built-up or bare a surface is, derived from Landsat and Sentinel-2 imagery in Google Earth Engine and reduced to a yearly median per municipality.
datasets.key_variables: NDBI (yearly median per municipality)
datasets.custodian: USGS (Landsat) and ESA (Sentinel-2), accessed through Google Earth Engine
datasets.producer: IPSP, computed in Google Earth Engine
datasets.licence: Landsat public domain; Sentinel-2 Copernicus licence
datasets.sharing_conditions: Derived series redistributable with attribution to USGS and ESA.
datasets.limitations: The sensor changes in 2017, so the 30 m and 10 m halves of the series are not directly comparable. Treat the break explicitly in any trend model.

datasets.title: Land surface temperature for urban heat islands
datasets.title_pt: Temperatura de superfície (LST) para ilhas de calor
datasets.description: Thermal satellite imagery giving surface temperature across the city, used to map the heat-island pattern between the sparse weather stations and to characterise every census sector.
datasets.key_variables: Land surface temperature; derived surface urban heat island intensity per census sector
datasets.custodian: USGS (Landsat 8/9) and NASA (MODIS), accessed through Google Earth Engine
datasets.native_resolution: 100 m thermal resampled to 30 m (Landsat); 1 km (MODIS)
datasets.temporal_resolution: 16-day revisit per satellite (about 8 days combined); MODIS twice daily
datasets.licence: Landsat public domain; NASA open data
datasets.sharing_conditions: Redistributable with attribution.
datasets.limitations: Surface temperature is not air temperature, and cloud cover removes many São Paulo summer scenes - exactly the season the dengue analysis cares about. Use as a spatial pattern to complement CLI-004, not as a substitute for it.

datasets.title: Terrain elevation and slope (SRTM)
datasets.description: Digital elevation model used to derive mean slope and relief range per municipality, as context for temperature and for vector habitat.
datasets.key_variables: Elevation; mean slope; relief range per municipality
datasets.custodian: NASA, accessed through AppEEARS
datasets.licence: NASA open data
datasets.sharing_conditions: Redistributable with attribution.
datasets.limitations: A single 2000 survey; no change over time. A municipality mean hides the range that matters in mountainous terrain.

datasets.title: WorldClim elevation (coarse backup)
datasets.description: Coarse global elevation layer held as a fallback. Retained in the catalogue for completeness and explicitly not used in the models.
datasets.key_variables: Elevation
datasets.custodian: WorldClim (University of California, Davis)
datasets.licence: CC BY-SA 4.0
datasets.sharing_conditions: Redistributable with attribution.
datasets.limitations: Too coarse for municipality-level work - superseded by ENV-005 and not used in any model.

datasets.title: Human footprint index, HIBR-10
datasets.description: Human Impact on the Brazilian Environment at 10 m resolution (HIBR-10): a national raster scoring human pressure on every 10 m cell from land cover, building density, and distance to major roads, railways and navigable waterways. It is the highest-resolution human footprint layer available for Brazil.
datasets.key_variables: Weighted human footprint score, 0-100 (rescaled from 0-10); component layers supplied separately
datasets.custodian: Zenodo deposit 10.5281/zenodo.15306587 (Hamilton & Presotto, 2025)
datasets.producer: Presotto A, Hamilton S, Izar P. A 10-meter resolution human footprint dataset to support biodiversity and conservation studies in Brazil. Scientific Data 2025;12:1754. doi:10.1038/s41597-025-06034-0
datasets.contact: Stuart Hamilton, East Carolina University (corresponding author)
datasets.spatial_coverage: Brazil, all biomes; clipped to State of Pará for this project
datasets.native_resolution: 10 m (86.5 billion cells), projected EPSG:5880 SIRGAS 2000 / Brazil Polyconic
datasets.analysis_unit: Municipality (zonal mean of the footprint score)
datasets.temporal_coverage: Static - built from 2023 Sentinel-2 land cover and post-2020 building footprints
datasets.update_frequency: By release version; the file is HFI_Weighted_vx.tif, higher x is a later release
datasets.licence: Article CC BY-NC-ND 4.0. Check the Zenodo deposit terms before redistributing any derived layer, since NC-ND would restrict it.
datasets.sharing_conditions: Cite Presotto et al. 2025 and the Zenodo DOI. Confirm the deposit licence before publishing a derived or reweighted layer.
datasets.limitations: NoData is coded 255, not null - set it explicitly or the zonal means are wrong. Scores are rescaled 0-100 from the published 0-10 scale. The aggregation weights (40% land cover, 40% building density, 10% major roads, 5% railways, 5% waterways) are the authors' choices for primate conservation; the authors intend users to reweight for their own question, which for ACL might mean raising forest-edge and waterway terms. A single snapshot, so no change over the 2000-2024 study period.

datasets.title: Satellite surface-water and flood extent
datasets.title_pt: Extensão de água superficial e inundação por satélite
datasets.description: Mapped water surface through time, from the JRC Global Surface Water record and MapBiomas Água. Together these give seasonal and permanent water extent per municipality, which is the closest thing to a real inundation layer without new field data.
datasets.key_variables: Water occurrence and seasonality; monthly water extent; flooded area per municipality-month
datasets.custodian: European Commission Joint Research Centre (JRC); MapBiomas project
datasets.producer: JRC Global Surface Water (Landsat); MapBiomas Água
datasets.contact: Google Earth Engine account; MapBiomas platform
datasets.spatial_coverage: Global (JRC) and Brazil (MapBiomas Água); subset State of Pará
datasets.analysis_unit: Municipality x month (flooded area and share of municipal area)
datasets.licence: JRC open data (CC BY 4.0); MapBiomas CC BY-SA 4.0
datasets.sharing_conditions: Redistributable with attribution to each product.
datasets.limitations: Optical sensors cannot see water under forest canopy or through Amazonian cloud, which is exactly when and where flooding matters. Treat as a lower bound. If canopy flooding proves important, radar (Sentinel-1) would be the next step, at a higher processing cost.
datasets.holding_status: Candidate - under assessment for the inundation layer

datasets.title: IBGE municipal boundaries
datasets.description: The official municipal boundary geometry. Every gridded climate and environmental layer is reduced to municipality values against this mesh, so it is the join that holds the whole catalogue together.
datasets.key_variables: Municipality polygon; 7-digit IBGE code; name; state; area
datasets.custodian: IBGE - Instituto Brasileiro de Geografia e Estatística
datasets.licence: Open government data, attribution to IBGE
datasets.sharing_conditions: Redistributable with attribution.
datasets.linkage_key: IBGE municipality code - 7-digit here, 6-digit in health files (cod6 = cod7 // 10)
datasets.limitations: Municipalities are created and boundaries change between editions, so long time series need a fixed reference year stated up front.

datasets.title: IBGE 2022 census - sector-level indicators
datasets.description: Population, income, household density and sanitation indicators at census-sector level, the finest official social geography available. Supplies both the denominator and the main confounders for the São Paulo heat-island analysis.
datasets.key_variables: Resident population; household density; income; water supply; sewerage connection; waste collection; sector polygon
datasets.custodian: IBGE
datasets.spatial_coverage: Brazil; subset municipality of São Paulo
datasets.update_frequency: Every 10 years, with staged releases of each indicator set
datasets.licence: Open government data, attribution to IBGE
datasets.sharing_conditions: Redistributable with attribution. Small-count suppression rules already applied by IBGE.
datasets.limitations: Sector boundaries changed between 2010 and 2022, so pre-2022 dengue years cannot be joined to 2022 sectors without an areal-interpolation step. A single snapshot cannot capture change across the 2015-2024 study window.

datasets.title: Static municipal environmental context
datasets.description: A fixed table of Köppen climate class, biome and altitude per municipality, used as unchanging context in the models.
datasets.key_variables: Köppen class; biome; altitude
datasets.custodian: InfoDengue Sprint 2024-25 environmental table
datasets.licence: To be confirmed
datasets.sharing_conditions: Confirm the InfoDengue redistribution terms before republishing.
datasets.limitations: One class per municipality flattens real internal variation in large municipalities.

datasets.title: Municipality zonal statistics and climate anomaly indicators
datasets.title_pt: Estatísticas zonais e indicadores de anomalia climática
datasets.description: The published municipality-level climate summaries and anomaly indicators produced by the laboratory, deposited on Zenodo so that others can reuse the processing rather than repeat it.
datasets.key_variables: Municipality zonal statistics for the ERA5-Land variables; anomaly indicators against the weekly normals
datasets.custodian: IPSP Climate and Health Laboratory; hosted by Zenodo
datasets.native_resolution: Derived from the ~9 km ERA5-Land grid
datasets.licence: As stated on the Zenodo record
datasets.sharing_conditions: Openly citable by DOI. Cite the deposit version used.
datasets.limitations: Fixed at the deposit date; re-run against current ERA5-Land for recent years.

datasets.title: Yellow fever exposure indicators
datasets.description: Exposure variables built from minimum temperature rather than downloaded: warm-night counts, warm spells and anomalies against the weekly normals. These are the actual model inputs.
datasets.key_variables: Days with Tmin above 17 C; runs of 7 or more consecutive warm days in April-September; Tmin anomaly against the 1981-2010 and 1991-2020 normals; extreme-rainfall weeks above the 99th percentile
datasets.custodian: IPSP Climate and Health Laboratory
datasets.access: Internal - to be published with the paper
datasets.licence: CC BY 4.0 proposed on publication
datasets.sharing_conditions: Shareable with collaborators now; deposit publicly at acceptance.
datasets.limitations: Thresholds (17 C, 7 days, 99th percentile) are analytical choices, not properties of the data - record the version used with every result. Flooding has no dataset and is approximated by extreme rainfall.

datasets.title: Leishmaniasis climate and vector indicators
datasets.description: Indicators built from temperature, rainfall and humidity for the ACL models, including a simple sand-fly population simulation. Relative humidity is computed from ERA5-Land dew-point using the same method as the yellow fever work.
datasets.key_variables: Relative humidity derived from 2 m dew-point and air temperature; seasonal temperature, rainfall and humidity anomalies (2000-2024 baseline); accumulated warmth above 10 C; favourable-infection flag (22-28 C and rainfall above 50 mm); simulated sand-fly density; 1-8 month lags; 3-month rolling mean of case counts
datasets.custodian: IPSP Climate and Health Laboratory
datasets.access: Internal - to be published with the paper
datasets.licence: CC BY 4.0 proposed on publication
datasets.sharing_conditions: Shareable with collaborators now; deposit publicly at acceptance.
datasets.limitations: The favourable-infection thresholds and the vector model are assumptions carried into every downstream result; document and sensitivity-test them. The 2000-2024 anomaly baseline is the study period itself, which shrinks apparent trends. Humidity is derived, not measured - validate against INMET stations (CLI-005).

field_definitions: Stable identifier. Prefix marks the domain: HEA health, CLI climate, ENV environment, REF reference geography, DER derived by the laboratory.
The name the dataset is known by, in English and Portuguese.
Health, Climate, Environment, Reference or Derived.
Which of the three research lines use this dataset. Datasets used by more than one project are the reason the catalogue is shared rather than per-project.
Plain-language description of the contents, written for someone who has not used the dataset.
The specific fields or bands actually used.
The organisation that controls access, which is not always the organisation that produced it.
The system or programme that generates the data.
Where to ask. A portal, a named division, or an account type.
The pixel size, station spacing or record granularity as distributed.
What one row becomes after processing. Almost everything here is reduced to one value per municipality or census sector.
The time step as distributed, and the step it is aggregated to.
How far behind real time the most recent usable record sits. This is the field that decides whether a dataset can support an operational decision.
Open, open with registration, by request, or restricted by agreement.
What must be in place before the data can be used or passed on: agreements, ethics approval, attribution, suppression rules, pre-publication review.
Whether the records identify or could identify individuals, and what must be done about it.
The field that joins this dataset to the others. Recording it is what makes the catalogue operational rather than descriptive.
What the dataset cannot tell you, stated before someone discovers it during analysis.
In use, held but unused, to be acquired, or a candidate under consideration.
Who is answerable for this record, at the institute that contributed it.
Verified, draft, or action needed. Draft records are entries where the description still needs confirmation from the holder.
